title: Wanting Approval vs. Needing Approval
headline: The Difference Between Wanting and Needing Approval
headline_sub: Approval Is a Wonderful Gift and a Terrible God
tagline: Approval is a wonderful gift. It is a terrible god.
seo_title: Wanting vs. Needing Approval: What the Bible Says (Galatians 1:10) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: God doesn't want us to stop caring about people. The problem begins when approval becomes necessary for our identity. A devotional on Galatians 1:10.
verse_text: For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.

scriptures.text: For am I now seeking the approval of man, or of God? Or am I trying to please man? If I were still trying to please man, I would not be a servant of Christ.

blocks.text: One of the greatest misconceptions Christians can have is believing that God wants us to stop caring about people.

items: He calls us to love our spouse.

blocks.text: Healthy relationships naturally include appreciation, affirmation, and mutual respect.

items: The problem begins when approval becomes necessary for our identity.
There is a profound difference between these two statements:

blocks.text: For example, someone might agree to take on extra work at their job, even when they are already overwhelmed, simply because they fear disappointing their boss. Another person might avoid having an honest conversation with a friend or spouse, choosing silence over truth because they are afraid of losing approval or acceptance. Or someone might constantly check social media, feeling uplifted or discouraged based on how many likes or comments they receive.
He was never controlled by the crowd because His identity had already been settled by His Father.

items: Before Jesus ever performed a miracle….
The Father declared, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
We spend our lives hoping performance will finally produce identity.
The crowd should never define you.

blocks.text: And here’s the truth that settles it: if God has already approved you in Christ, then no amount of human applause can add to you, and no amount of rejection can take anything away.

items: Whose opinion has the greatest emotional influence over me?
When criticism comes, what does it reveal about what I’m trusting?
Do I revert to old default reactions because of past wounds?
Am I enjoying encouragement, or am I depending on it?
Thank You that my identity was never meant to rest in human applause.
Teach me to receive encouragement without becoming dependent upon it.
Help me enjoy relationships without making them my source of worth.
May Your voice become louder than every other voice.
